items.claim: The row's textual analysis is accurate but its rationale narrates pipeline structure ('this same writer part') instead of citing verses only, a register violation.
items.evidence: Rationale states the Prov.14.27 repetition falls 'later in this same writer part' -- 'writer part' is file-order/pipeline language the campaign register purge bans from row prose (cross-row references must be verse-anchored, not positional). The underlying textual claims are independently correct and the repetition is stronger than 'word for word' suggests -- it is byte-identical: 13:14's closing clause לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת and 14:27's closing clause לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת match at the byte tier (identical bytes including cantillation, verified against each verse's own oshb text); sweep.py confirms this exact clause occurs at exactly 2 verses book-wide (13:14, 14:27, skeleton tier) and the phrase מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים occurs at exactly 4 verses (10:11, 13:14, 14:27, 16:22, skeleton tier) -- both matching the row's counts exactly. single_proverb and parent_collection C2 are correct; no undisclosed cross-seam device with 13:13 or 13:15 (no shared content token at skeleton tier with either neighbor).

items.claim: The cluster's catchword evidence is real, but the row uses banned file-order phrasing twice and its rejected_alternative does not test a genuine rival.
items.evidence: Rationale narrates 'the tongue-noun pairing earlier in this part (Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19)' and rejected_alternative narrates the cluster carries 'the same reduced confidence as the range's other thin catchword pairing' -- 'this part' / 'the range's' is pipeline/file-order talk banned from row prose by the register purge; the second instance also fails the verse-anchored requirement for cross-row reference (no verse is named there). Separately, the rejected_alternative only restates the confidence calibration rather than testing why single_proverb might be the stronger reading given a single shared token -- a thin, largely circular rival rather than the strongest real one. The underlying cluster evidence itself is genuine: כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים (13:19) and כְסִילִ֣ים (13:20) are the identical plural fools-noun opening the B-colon predicate in both verses (parallel-slot catchword, skeleton tier), matching the row's own account; the right-hand seam (13:20/13:21) is independently guarded by the sibling row's homograph disclosure. medium_low confidence is a fair calibration for one-token cohesion.

items.claim: The antithesis reading and the 13:20 homograph disclosure are sound, but the row omits a byte-confirmed catchword chain at its own right-hand seam with 13:22.
items.evidence: The last word of 13:21 (טֽוֹב, byte tier from oshb) and the first word of 13:22 (ט֗וֹב, byte tier from oshb) are the same word at accent_stripped tier (the two byte forms differ only in cantillation accent, expected since they sit in different metrical positions) -- an anadiplosis at the verse seam -- and the two verses further share the root pair צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים/לַ֝צַּדִּ֗יק ('righteous') and חַ֭טָּאִים/חוֹטֵֽא ('sinner'). Governance treats an undisclosed byte-true device straddling a row's own seam as arguing continuity unless disclosed; this row discloses only the homograph with 13:20 (correctly) and says nothing about the stronger, multi-root echo on its other side. This does not overturn the antithetic single_proverb call -- each verse is independently closed by its own waw-antithesis -- but the echo needed disclosure as texture, the same standard applied at the 14:6/14:7 knowledge-noun seam.

items.claim: The row correctly places 13:22 in the tov-opener class but misses that its own opening word repeats the closing word of the bordering verse, 13:21.
items.evidence: 13:22 opens with ט֗וֹב (byte tier, oshb); 13:21 closes with טֽוֹב (byte tier, oshb) -- the same word at accent_stripped tier (the two byte forms differ only in cantillation, expected across different metrical slots) -- an undisclosed anadiplosis at the row's own left-hand seam, compounded by the shared roots לַ֝צַּדִּ֗יק/צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים ('righteous') and חוֹטֵֽא/חַ֭טָּאִים ('sinner') across the same two verses. The row's own rationale already discusses 13:22's tov-opener form (correctly distinguishing it from a tov-min comparative, matching prov_device_inventory.json's tov_openers list, which does list Prov.13.22) yet does not extend that discussion one clause to its left. The atomic call still holds under the antithetic-waw test, but the cross-seam device is undisclosed.

items.claim: single_proverb is correct and the lexical crux on the tillage-owner noun is honestly disclosed rather than resolved.
items.evidence: MT ראשים is genuinely ambiguous between 'heads/chiefs' and the sense WEB renders 'poor people' -- the row correctly flags this as a gloss not transparent from the bare consonants, and correctly notes no morphology layer is staged to resolve it (matches TOOLKIT.md's explicit no-morphology-layer disclaimer). No subject-vs-subject antithesis is present -- the same topic (the field's produce) runs through both cola -- so the synthetic-shape reasoning for single_proverb is defensible under the same subject-continuity test used at 13:14. Skeleton comparison against both neighbors (13:22, 13:24) shows no shared content token with either, so no undisclosed cross-seam device is missed. Register is clean -- no file-order or positional language.

items.claim: The petuchah and antithesis claims are byte-accurate and correctly governed, but the row's file-order phrasing violates the register purge.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json confirms Prov.13.25 is the sole PE/SAMEKH mark across chapters 12-14 (matching prov_device_inventory.json's parashah_distribution count of 1 for chapter 13), and 13:25 does close chapter 13 -- both claims check out, and the row correctly treats the mark as tier-3 single-witness corroboration rather than a driver, consistent with governance. However the rationale calls it 'the range's one disclosed petuchah' -- 'the range' is the same file-order/pipeline phrasing (denoting the writer's assigned span rather than a verse-anchored unit) that recurs elsewhere in this writer's rows and is banned from row prose; 'chapter 13's' would have been register-clean and was available two clauses later in the same sentence.

items.claim: The imperative-mood observation, the בל cross-reference to 12:3, and the rejection of admonition_unit reclassification are all accurate and well-grounded.
items.evidence: לך (14:7) is a genuine Qal imperative opening, a real mood shift from the surrounding declaratives. The negative particle בַּל closing 14:7 (as וּבַל) does recur in 12:3's B-colon (בַּל יִמּֽוֹט) -- confirmed by direct token comparison of both verses -- a legitimate, verse-anchored cross-reference. The rejected_alternative correctly applies the section-6 policy: C2's atomic default holds regardless of a verse's imperative mood, and no collection seam falls at 14:7 (it sits well inside C2, Prov.10.1-22.16, far from the 22:17 admonition-unit territory). The row also discloses its own left-hand seam correctly: 14:6 (וְדַ֖עַת) and 14:7 (דָֽעַת) share the exact noun 'knowledge' as ordinary vocabulary, not a construction run -- the disclosure standard this cluster's other rows sometimes omit. Register is clean throughout.

items.claim: The cluster's core catchword evidence is strong and byte-confirmed, but the row's rejected_alternative violates register with a non-verse-anchored file-order reference.
items.evidence: 14:12's וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ and 14:13's וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ ('and its end/latter part', both byte tier from oshb) are the same word at accent_stripped tier (byte forms differ only in cantillation, expected for differing metrical position), occupying the same B-colon-opening slot in both verses -- a genuine construction-level catchword, stronger evidence than a merely-shared noun. However the rejected_alternative closes by saying the pair carries more weight 'than the range's thinner one-token catchword pairs' -- this both uses banned file-order language ('the range') and fails the verse-anchored cross-reference requirement (the alluded-to pairing is never named by verse). Boundary check on both sides: 14:11/14:12 share only the common root יְשָׁרִ֣ים/יָ֭שָׁר (book-wide high-frequency, low distinctiveness) and 14:13/14:14 share only לֵ֑ב/לֵ֑ב ('heart', likewise high-frequency) -- neither rises to the level of the row's own אחריתה evidence, so the cluster's own boundaries hold.
